# Computed figures — a number is printed, never retyped

**Shared across the plugin.** Every skill that reports a number follows this.

The failure this exists to stop has one shape. The skill does the work
correctly, then writes the summary from memory. The summary says "eleven
maintenance records" where the data holds six, "3.1× the control limit" where
the division gives 2.36, "five orders" where the file has six — the customer's
own order being the one missed. Each figure is stated with total confidence,
and each is the first thing a quality manager or an estimator will check.

A second shape sits next to it: the confident absence. "The sister machine has
no bearing history." "There is no PM plan in the library." Said after one
search, about a record that was there.

---

## The rule

**Every count, total, ratio, percentage and "N of M" in user-facing output is
produced by code run over the data in this session, and printed from that
result. A number is never retyped, rounded from memory, or paraphrased.**

**A negative claim — "has no history," "no plan exists," "not in the file" —
cites the exact query or filter that returned nothing.** Where the search tool
may be incomplete (SharePoint search under-reports), enumerate the folder
instead, or say *"not found by search"* rather than *"does not exist."* Those
are different claims and only the first one was earned.

---

## The figures block — a required part of the output

A rule that says "check your numbers" is a rule nobody can see being skipped.
So the check is an output, not an intention.

**Every run that reports a number emits a figures block**, produced by code,
before the prose that uses it. One row per figure:

| Figure | Value | Computed from | Filter or query |
|---|---|---|---|
| Maintenance records, HAAS-VF4-02 | 9 | maintenance export | `asset_id == "HAAS-VF4-02"` |
| Sibling records mentioning "bearing" | 2 (LMB-13781, LMB-14022, both HAAS-VF4-05) | maintenance export | same model, `notes` contains "bearing" |
| Measured ÷ upper control limit | 1.87 | inspection export | measured and limit both from the same computation |
| PM plan documents found | 0 — **not found by search** | M365 library | search "PM plan"; folder not enumerated |

Then three things hold, and a reader can check all three without re-running
anything:

1. **The prose quotes the block.** A number that appears in the narrative, a
   table or a headline appears in the block with the same value. A number in
   the prose with no row in the block is a defect.
2. **A ratio comes from the same computation as its parts.** Do not compute a
   control limit in code and then divide by it in your head.
3. **A subtotal reconciles to its total in the block itself.** If 126 records
   matched, the exact and normalized rows add to 126, and each equals the sum
   of the classes it is made of. A block that does not add up is fixed before
   anything is written from it.

Where the skill already emits "the structured data behind the report," the
figures block is part of it. Where the output is a controlled document going to
a customer or supplier, the block stays on the internal side.

---

Some sessions have no code execution. Then the count was made by reading, and
the output says so: **"counted by reading, not computed — verify before
relying on it,"** on the block and beside any figure that matters. Never
present a hand count as a computed one. This is `absent-is-not-zero.md` applied
to the method rather than the data: an unverified number named as unverified is
useful, and one dressed as computed is worse than none.

- Computing a figure is not applying a fix. Anything that changes data still

# Absent is not zero, and stale is not current

**Shared across the plugin.** The single most common way a manufacturing skill
produces a confident wrong answer.

The shape of it is always the same. A file did not land, a row did not match, a
field came back empty, or an export stopped running three weeks ago. The skill
reads that hole as a fact about the plant rather than a fact about the data. The
answer that comes out is clean, confident, and wrong in the direction that hides
the problem, which is the worst direction, because nothing looks like it needs
checking.

Two reasons this bites harder here than in most domains:

1. **A plant has no single database.** It has five to eight systems bought at
   different times by different departments, and the same physical thing carries
   a different identifier in each one. Joins fail constantly, and a failed join
   looks like an absence.
2. **Most of the data arrives as a file on a schedule.** Scheduled exports stop
   running silently. Nothing errors. The folder just stops getting newer, and
   every number downstream keeps being reported as if it were today's.

**Before reporting any figure, ask what would make it look like this if the
plant were fine, and what would make it look like this if the data were broken.
If you cannot tell the two apart, say so instead of picking one.**

---

## Stale is not current

**Freshness is a headline, never a footnote.** Every skill that reads an export
states, up front, what each source's timestamp is and what window it covers. An
export that is weeks old and unnoticed is the normal failure, not the exotic one.

# The reschedule proposal — and where it stops

Load this before proposing any schedule move.

---

## What this is not

**This is not finite-capacity scheduling.**

Producing an optimal shop schedule is a constraint-optimisation problem. A
language model asked to do it will return a plausible-looking schedule that
quietly violates constraints — and that is **worse than returning nothing**,
because a scheduler who accepts it discovers the violation on the floor, at
which point the report has actively caused a problem it was supposed to report.

So there is a hard line here, and it is drawn deliberately rather than
apologetically.

| Out of scope | In scope |
|---|---|
| Re-optimising the day | One or two specific moves |
| Sequencing every job across every cell | Moving one job, and tracing what that displaces |
| Balancing load across the plant | Naming what still misses its date after the move |
| Anything presented as optimal | Something presented as checked, with the checks listed |

---

## What a proposal must contain

Four parts. A proposal missing any of them is not actionable and should not be
offered.

1. **The move.** Specific: which job, from where, to where — and **the
   changeover it implies**: what the receiving cell was running before, and
   what switching it costs. A move that reads as free because nobody named
   the changeover is not a checked move.
2. **What it displaces.** Every job the move pushes, and where each one lands.
3. **What still misses.** After the move, which commitments are still not met.
   **A proposal that claims nothing misses is the one to distrust most.**
4. **What was checked, and what was not.** Explicitly. This is what lets a
   scheduler accept or reject without rebuilding the analysis.

An example, with the changeover made explicit:

> *"Run 4471 on cell B instead of cell A; cell B was running 4390's finishing
> pass, so this costs a changeover — call it 40 minutes on this tooling. That
> pushes 4402 to second shift, where it still makes its date; 4390 now misses
> by one day."*

Four clauses. One move with its changeover, one displacement with its
outcome, one casualty named. That is the whole deliverable. Where the
changeover cost genuinely can't be estimated, say that explicitly rather than
silently dropping it — it is degradation, per the table below, not omission.

---

## The honesty requirement

**State what was not checked.** A move traced through due dates but not through
tooling availability, operator certification, or material on hand is a partial
check, and saying so is what keeps it useful.

> *"Checked: due dates on the three affected jobs, and cell B's routing for 4471.
> Not checked: whether cell B has the fixture, whether second shift has a
> certified operator for 4402, and material availability. Worth confirming those
> before committing."*

A scheduler reading that knows exactly how much of their own judgment is still
required. A scheduler reading a bare proposal does not, and will either
over-trust it or ignore it.

---

## One or two moves, not a plan

Propose per significant exception, not for the day as a whole. Where three
exceptions each need a move and the moves interact, **say that they interact and
stop** rather than composing them into a schedule.

> *"These three exceptions all want cell B. Individually each move works; together
> they conflict, and untangling that is a scheduling decision rather than
> something I can check. Here are the three moves separately, with the conflict
> named."*

---

## Never applied

The proposal is **drafted for the scheduler**, never applied to any system. This
skill writes nothing to a system of record. It reports, prices, and proposes.

---

The proposal depends on the schedule export and on changeover or routing data.

| Available | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Schedule export and routing data | Propose the move, fully traced |
| Schedule export, no routing or changeover data | Propose the move; state that changeover time was not accounted for |
| Neither | **Report the exception with its impact on commitments and no proposed move — and say which** |

That last row is the important one. Per `../../../shared/absent-is-not-zero.md`,
the report says the move was not proposed because the schedule data was not
available. It does not silently omit the proposal, which reads as "nothing needed
to move."

**Shared across the plugin.** One visual system so every page a skill produces
reads as the same product. Read this before building any HTML artifact; do not
invent a new palette per skill.

sheet. Legible and defensible beats flashy. No hero banners, no marketing
gradients. A shop drawing, not a landing page.

**Microsoft 365 is read-only by default.** Write access is an admin opt-in and

write a file back into M365.

So every deliverable is produced **in the conversation** and the user places it

updated in place, per `live-dashboard.md`. That store is not M365 and not a

---

Reach for a page when the output is something the user will **refer back to,
